descriptionChirho: The Mosaic Law, the Torah of YHWH, divine covenant legislation, or 'the Law' as a body of authoritative divine instruction — including all inflected forms with article, possessive suffixes (Your/My/His law when referring to God), construct chains (Torah-of Moses, law-of YHWH), and prepositional prefixes (in/from/according-to the Torah).

Teaching, instruction, or direction given by a parent, sage, priest, or prophet — the word's original sense of guidance/pointing (from ירה), used especially in Proverbs for parental wisdom instruction and in prophetic literature for priestly rulings, as distinct from the formal Mosaic covenant code.

The plural form תּוֹרֹת (torot) referring to specific laws, regulations, statutes, or sets of divine instructions — used for individual legal prescriptions (especially ritual laws in Leviticus) or collectively for God's commandments as distinct enactments rather than as a unified Torah.
